title: Law 4: Say Less Than Necessary to Guard Focus
hook: Over-explaining is an anxiety response that surrenders leverage.
core_insight: Robert Greene's 4th Law of Power dictates that powerful people impress and intimidate by saying less. ADHD often manifests in high-stakes rooms as verbal processing—over-explaining to validate competence or resolve awkward silence. Silence projects poise, forces others to reveal their motives, and drastically conserves working memory. Let concise outputs carry the burden of proof.
takeaways: State the technical conclusion in one sentence, then embrace the silence.
Treat speech as a scarce resource: excess words provide attack surfaces and bleed leverage.
external_reference: Robert Greene, 48 Laws of Power, Law 4
